transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sasha Kaplan, Marco Diaz, Priya Nair, Owen Park, Jules Laurent, Maya Chen + all staff dialed in

Summary:
Sasha opened with context-setting: focus this quarter is execution rigor + living our values when tradeoffs arise. Short updates from Product, Eng, People, Growth. Half of the meeting used for Q&A; a few candid moments about hiring, SLOs, and competitor moves.

Topics:
- H2 product prioritization approach and pilot gating
- Operational SLOs: latency vs cost tradeoffs and when to favor reliability
- Hiring cadence + interview loop changes
- PLG conversion experiments and growth asks
- Values in hard decisions (customer privacy, cut features vs quality)

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Sasha: ok, hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Saturday—no, joking—on a Thursday. Um 16:00, we're gonna keep this tight. Two big things: execution and values. I'm gonna go quick updates then we open to q and a. Marco, quick infra note?
[00:22] Marco: yeah thanks Sasha. So infra, we're seeing stable node utilization at 63% across prod, small bump after the routing patch. There was a missed regression in the kv cache warmup that slowed cold starts on some workloads, we rolled a hotfix yesterday. Sorry about the noise.
[00:40] Owen: to add, the hotfix reduced 99th percentile cold-start by ~120ms in our internal tests, but we did notice a 1.2% increase in cost on p50 per policy because of more eager caching for short sessions.
[01:05] Priya: product update—thanks team. Quick headline: we narrowed H2 pilot set to three features: smart-routing priority for tiered customers, chained function/tool-calls for structured outputs, and an embeddings prefetch cache experiment. We're gating on clear success metrics and a 6-week pilot timeline.
[01:30] Sasha: great. One thing I want to emphasize: these pilots are as much about learnings as revenue; if a pilot reduces latency for a key cohort but spikes cost, we need to see the ROI. Don't bury tradeoffs.
[01:48] Jules: hiring note—interview loop changes start next week. We're removing one hiring panel step for IC levels, streamlining take-home assignments, and tightening score calibration. Early data shows faster time-to-offer by 18% in pilot teams.
[02:10] Maya: growth—PLG experiments: we've rolled a new onboarding prompt template to 12% of new orgs, conversion to first API call up 9 points. We want product to give a short list of toggles that help with conversion without raising costs.
[02:35] Sasha: ok let's open to q and a, but quick rules: candid, specific asks, and if it's operational let's ping the owners after.

[03:00] Employee 1 (via Q): hi—question about prioritized roadmap, will the pilots be exclusive to hosted API or also Dedicated/Private?
[03:20] Priya: short answer: pilots will be staged. Hosted first for speed, Dedicated next for scale validation, and Private only if the pilot requires on-prem drivers or particular KMS integrations. We want parity but not at once; that increases blast radius.
[03:45] Employee 2: about SLOs, do we have guardrails when cost optimization can degrade tail latency for paid customers?
[04:05] Sasha: yep this is core. We will set customer-tier SLOs that cannot be auto-optimized away. Any cost-driven routing changes must have an opt-out for gold/platinum customers and a rollback window. Owen?
[04:22] Owen: adding to that—our plan is to introduce a routing policy config in the console: 'latency-first', 'cost-first', 'balanced'. We'll default enterprise to 'latency-first'. We need clarity on metrics we show in the UI so customers can pick intentionally.
[04:45] Employee 3: quick—competitor question, heard rumor Anthropic is doing something similar with prefix caching—should we be worried?
[05:00] Marco: public signals indicate they're focusing on research-level pref, but our strength is production runtime and observability. Keep watching but don't chase every paper. We should do kernel-level experiments that show delta at scale.

[05:22] Sasha: ok, I'm gonna pivot to a short case: last week a customer asked for aggressive price cuts in exchange for a 2-year commit. Our values conversation came up: do we compromise latency or invest in capacity? We decided: we can't degrade reliability for commit revenue. We proposed a tiered plan with burst credits instead. That kept SLA and allowed the commit.
[06:00] Employee 4: follow up—how do we say no to revenue in a way that doesn't burn bridges?
[06:15] Sasha: empathetic no. Offer alternatives that preserve core guarantees. Document the decision rationale in the deal ticket so AE/Sales can reference it.

[06:40] Priya: back to pilots—metrics we care about: activation to first API call, 7-day retention, per-token cost delta, p95/p99 tail latency delta, and support volume change. We'll publish a small template for pilot metrics later today.
[07:05] Maya: and growth asks product for a small 'experiment channel' inside the console so we can segment cohorts per org, that's a low-effort UI change.
[07:22] Owen: on infra, quick ask—we need product to sign off on more aggressive batching heuristics for internal alpha. The risk is wider latency variance. We need a written playbook for rollback.
[07:45] Priya: agree. We'll provide a decision memo that outlines acceptable variance thresholds and rollback steps.

[08:10] Sasha: ok switching to People. Jules?
[08:15] Jules: hiring is accelerating; two asks: 1) leadership calibration sessions next Wed to reduce score variance, and 2) more interviewers in infra/serving runtime. We'll run a brief training workshop.
[08:35] Employee 5: question about comp bands and market movement?
[08:45] Jules: we're re-benchmarking against market and will share a mid-year compensation note. No immediate freezes, but we are optimizing offers to close key roles faster.

[09:05] Sasha: now open floor—please be concise.
[09:15] Employee 6: Metrics ask—can we get a dashboard showing per-route cost and top offending prompts?
[09:30] Marco: yes we have a prototype in Observability lab; not ready for prod but we can share a demo next week.
[09:48] Employee 7: Can we have clearer docs about which features are GA vs experimental to reduce support tickets?
[10:05] Priya: on it—publishing a one-pager and a console badge for experimental vs GA.

[10:30] Sasha: two candid notes before we close: 1) hiring is our #1 constraint—everyone can help by interviewing, and 2) when in doubt pick the customer guarantee over short-term efficiency unless there's a clear ROI.
[10:55] Owen: operational note—we'll run a 48-hour quality bake this month where batches are tuned in dark traffic to surface regressions. Expect some noise in internal dashboards.
[11:15] Sasha: ok recap of next steps: Priya memo, Owen SLO proposal, Marco kernel notes, Jules hiring docs. We'll reconvene with PLG and Sales leads for a focused 30-min on Tuesday week.
[11:38] Maya: one last plug—growth will share the onboarding templating kit; if teams have feature flags they'd like to try in the 12% cohort, ping growth.
[11:55] Sasha: thanks all, back to heads of teams to run the playbooks and designers to keep things simple. End.

Notes on transcription quality: automated transcript had a few misheard acronyms (e.g., 'kv cache' sometimes 'kv cash'), and speaker overlap on the Q&A portion. We kept the raw speech cadence when possible.
